assumptions: gearbox: the core's point evaluation with the torque given at the OUTPUT (torque_at='output', forward); the motor input speed is the output speed times the absolute overall ratio

coverage basis (covered_by_saved_point): one saved motor point, not a map. A row is covered when the required motor shaft torque AND speed are both not above the saved point's; between points nothing is claimed

chain efficiency (motor x gearbox) is given only when the required point matches the saved motor point within 2 % in torque AND speed; otherwise it is null (motor_point_differs). The two parts are always given separately, each with the point it belongs to; nothing from another point is multiplied silently

motor torque basis: when the saved summary carries the shaft_convention marker, the marked shaft quantity (coupling torque when a bearing model exists, else T_shaft_Nm); otherwise the field torque of the legacy convention (torque_basis: field_legacy)

gearbox losses are the core's stage results; a loss the core did not compute (bearings without bearing definitions, grease churning without a drag torque) is null with loss_inputs_missing, and the totals and the gearbox efficiency of that row are marked partial
total mass = saved motor mass (full assembled mass when the catalogue can weigh the motor, else the active mass) + gearbox analytical mass
core_limitations: motoring only: power flows motor -> load; reverse / regeneration is not computed
screening estimate, not a measured or certified rating; see docs/gear_module/CORE_API_AND_LIMITATIONS.md

loss by stage is the core's own estimate: mesh-loss correlation, bearing friction and churning are not qualified against measurements; a loss the core could not compute for lack of inputs (bearing definitions, grease drag torque) is null with loss_inputs_missing and the totals are marked partial
internal-root bending, signed-reversal fatigue and thin-rim gates are unsupported; a point result is never a qualification
mass and inertia of the gearbox are analytical blank estimates
